mechanism_narrative: A continuing decline in TRANSIT lagged into retail footfall will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks because fewer transit-linked trips imply more discretionary local shopping and dining near home. The signal is valid only if the transit drop is not matched by a sharper fall in WORKPLACES.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four weeks while TRANSIT remains depressed and WORKPLACES is flat or improving.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays above its recent level while GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline, households are shifting time toward home and nearby errands, which should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if residential time falls back or if grocery trips spike as a compensating outside-home activity.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above baseline and GROCERY_PHARM remaining close to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-on-week drop in PARKS below the recent trough will coincide with weaker discretionary out-of-home activity and reduce RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks. This is a short-lag signal because park visits are a near-term proxy for general leisure mobility.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15 after being above that threshold for at least one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 14 days after PARKS crosses below -15 and stays there.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply depressed while WORKPLACES is also below baseline, the shared reduction in commuting and office-linked trips suppresses retail spillovers, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. If WORKPLACES improves despite weak transit, the retail effect should disappear.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40 and WORKPLACES stays below -15 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next month even though TRANSIT stays below -40 and WORKPLACES stays below -15.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week improvement in GROCERY_PHARM above baseline can spill over into broader errand-making and nearby shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The effect should be small and short-lived if PARKS and TRANSIT do not also improve.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM turns positive.

mechanism_narrative: During reopening, rising PARKS and TRANSIT together indicate broader leisure and movement normalization, which should push RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks through higher spontaneous shopping trips. The effect is conditional on WORKPLACES not falling further.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next month while PARKS and TRANSIT both rise and WORKPLACES does not weaken.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline from its recent elevated level and TRANSIT keeps recovering, the city is exiting stay-at-home behavior and retail visits should increase over the next two weeks. The signal fails if residential time stays elevated or transit recovery stalls.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 6 while TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL falls below 6 and TRANSIT posts two weekly gains.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT should raise weekday retail demand by restoring lunch, commute, and after-work purchases, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. This mechanism is strongest only when RESIDENTIAL does not rise at the same time.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its prior four-week mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve and RESIDENTIAL does not increase.
